2606.11169.COMMENT: Decouples parallelism strategy from runtime by compiling annotations and scheduling directives over a global training DAG IR, reproducing DualPipe-style composed expert/pipeline schedules with joint compute-communication scheduling.
2606.11169.TOPIC_MATCH_COMMENT: It is a distributed training system whose contribution is composable data/pipeline/expert parallelism and ZeRO-style sharding as programmable IR transformations.
2606.11169.HOTSPOT_PAPER_COMMENT: Broadly important today: Decouples parallelism strategy from runtime by compiling annotations and scheduling directives over a global training DAG IR, reproducing DualPipe-style composed expert/pipeline schedules with joint compute-communication scheduling.
2606.11169.title: Piper: A Programmable Distributed Training System
2606.11169.abstract: Large-scale model training increasingly relies on composing multiple parallelism strategies, such as data, pipeline, and expert parallelism, together with memory-saving optimizations like ZeRO. Deployed systems for foundation model pretraining often rely on human experts to manually design a high-level parallelism strategy then implement the corresponding low-level execution strategy, making it difficult to adapt the system to new strategies. Meanwhile, many general-purpose frameworks are more flexible but their implementations are still tied to a fixed set of common parallelism strategies, making it challenging to integrate state-of-the-art strategies. We present Piper, a user-controllable distributed training system that decouples the strategy from the runtime implementation. Piper allows users to declare a comprehensive distributed training strategy with a small set of model annotations and scheduling directives. Each directive applies a transformation on Piper's intermediate representation (IR), a unified global training DAG that represents all computation and communication. Using this IR, Piper compiles per-device execution plans and executes them with a distributed runtime agnostic to the strategy. We show that the combined system maintains performance parity on commonly available strategies such as ZeRO, while also enabling additional performance and memory efficiency gains through joint scheduling of compute and communication in composed parallelism strategies such as DeepSeek-V3's DualPipe.

2606.10944.COMMENT: Converts a non-causal attention approximation into a causal one with matching guarantees, reaching log^{3/2}(n)/s error at O(s) memory, with an I/O-aware Triton kernel that beats FlashAttention 2.
2606.10944.TOPIC_MATCH_COMMENT: A causal attention mechanism with provable approximation bounds plus a real kernel is core architectural work; the prefill, KV-compression and memory-constrained decoding wins are downstream of that mechanism.
2606.10944.HOTSPOT_PAPER_COMMENT: Provable causal attention guarantees paired with measured speedups over FlashAttention 2 is a result the broader community will want to see the day it lands.
2606.10944.title: Express Language Modeling
2606.10944.abstract: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.
